items.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 open-weight listings diverge on parameter count — most third-party aggregators cite 552B total / 16B active, but Neura News reports Hugging Face safetensors show ~748.5B for backbone + engram alone and ~763B with MTP and vision included; provider pricing splits 2–4x; MIT license on Hugging Face is the one consistent fact
items.summary: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is the Chinese open-weight anchor that this week's model comparisons keep leaning on — including the MiniMax M3.1 Flash launch coverage in today's am, where Automation-Bench 62.2 vs V4.1 Flash-1017 60.5 and DeepSWE v1.1 73.7 vs V4.1 Flash-1017 77.0 are both vendor-reported numbers quoting the same V4.1 Flash model. Pm-window reads of the open-weight landscape surface a parameter-count discrepancy that is worth pinning down. Most third-party listings (Requesty, Gradually.ai, GetDeploying, DataLearner) describe V4.1 Flash as 552B total with 16B active. Neura News, citing Hugging Face safetensors directly, reports ~748.5B parameters for backbone + engram and roughly 763B once MTP and vision components are included — and references a Reddit thread arguing the real total is 748B, not 552B. Checkpoint size figures also split: one source reports ~314 GB at 4-bit for self-hosting, Neura News reports ~511.76 GB. Benchmark anchors do not fully agree either — Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 40 at $0.27/task; Requesty lists 39.5%. Pricing diverges across gateways: Requesty $0.30 input / $1.20 output per million tokens, another aggregator $0.15 / $0.60 off-peak, a third $0.22 / $0.66 at the cheapest listed provider — i.e. a 2–4x spread on the same model. The MIT license and open Hugging Face publication are the single consistent facts across every source. No DeepSeek-hosted technical report or vendor pricing page was reachable from this run (DNS continued to be inconsistent for direct WebFetch), so the full-text model card at huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is the one place to resolve the parameter count directly.
items.why_it_matters: This is the open-weight version of the am's running MiniMax theme — 'what has actually shipped' when third-party pages and vendor framing do not line up. For a Python workflow that would call this model through an API gateway, two practical reads. First, the parameter count figure that matters for self-hosting planning is the one in the safetensors on Hugging Face, not the number aggregators repeat from the vendor press release. If the backbone + engram alone is ~748.5B, the GPU memory footprint for a self-hosted 4-bit run is closer to 500 GB than 300 GB, and that changes whether a single-node setup is even on the table versus a multi-GPU rig. Not Gabe's immediate problem — self-hosting a 500 GB checkpoint from a Python script is not the beginner path — but the general lesson applies to every open-weight model: pull the safetensors metadata before planning around any third-party listing. Second, the gateway pricing split (2–4x across providers for the same MIT-licensed model) is the kind of thing that quietly adds up on a hobbyist budget. The lowest listed per-million-token price on this model is roughly $0.15 input / $0.60 output off-peak — identical to the bracket MiniMax M3.1 Flash is being quoted at — but one gateway shows $0.30 / $1.20 for the same model. For a 'cheap-and-measure' trial on three real tasks the way the am recommends for M3.1 Flash, pulling a key from the gateway that lists the specific model-ID string from the Hugging Face card (not a renamed variant) and verifying the per-token price before scripting is the practical move. The broader read for the week: both of this week's cheap Chinese agent-tier models (MiniMax M3.1 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017) have the same hygiene problem — vendor-cited specs get re-published downstream faster than any audit happens — and both reward checking the primary artifact (Hugging Face card, safetensors metadata, provider pricing page) over the aggregator summary.
items.why_it_matters_brief: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash safetensors reportedly show ~748B (not the vendor-cited 552B) and gateway pricing splits 2–4x — the open-weight version of this week's 'what has actually shipped' question.

takes.source: DataLearner — DeepSeek V4.1 Flash analysis page
takes.take: Independent coding-benchmark anchor. Ranks V4.1 Flash first on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (90.6) and first on CodeForces (3471) among 21 tracked models; DeepSWE 74.2 places it second of 38. Note that this is Terminal-Bench 2.1, a different version than Terminal-Bench 4.0 cited in MiniMax M3.1 Flash's launch table (38.1) — direct cross-reads between the two Chinese models on terminal-coding workloads are not clean.

takes.source: Artificial Analysis — DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model page
takes.take: Independent anchor. Intelligence Index 40 at $0.27/task. Vals ranks V4.1 Flash the top open-weight model on its index, per Neura News's secondary citation. The $0.27/task figure is the one that lets a cheap-and-measure trial from a Python script be budgeted directly against MiniMax M3.1 Flash's roughly comparable $0.15/$0.60 bracket.
